pr_body:
Fixes #49583

Requested by community: it's hard/inconvenient to program
orchestration with the `node decommission` command because
the orchestrator is not aware of crdb node IDs -- only pod
addresses. Therefore, it is useful to make these node commands operate
"on the node they are connected to".

Release note (cli change): The commands `cockroach node decommission`
and `recommission` now recognize a new flag `--self`. This can be
passed *in lieu* of an explicit list of node IDs, and indicates
that the operation targets the node the command is connected to
(either via `--host` if specified, or `localhost`).
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/50532)

@bdarnell can you review the discussion in #49583 - whether we should use an explicit flag `--self` or instead consider that the absence of node IDs is a request to target the local node.

Despite the argument "this way mistakes can be prevented", I feel icky about the lack of symmetry with `quit`, `init` etc for which the absence of a node ID is already a request to target the local node. WDYT?
Thanks ben for the feedback. This means the PR is good for review then?

issue_context.title: cli: make `cockroach node decommission` derive the target node ID from --host
issue_context.body:
Today `node decommission` requires an explicit list of node IDs on the command line.

It would be good if the command, like `cockroach node drain` and others, when provided no node ID explicitly, would automatically target the node that it's connected to (via `--host`).
comments: +1 to this, I was gonna open the same request. How to grab the local process's ID in an automated fashion (in order to then provide it as an argument to a `decommission` command) is surprisingly non-obvious. It'd be much easier if both `decommission` and `recommission` offered an easy way to target just the process being connected to.

Could this just be changed to add a `--self` flag that will target the local node ID?  Right now `node decommission` requires a list of node IDs:

```
cockroach node decommission <node IDs> <flags>
```

but it'd be really nice if you could call:

```
cockroach node decommission --self <flags>
```

and have this be a valid invocation that way a node can self-decommission when a shutdown signal is received for a given instance.

My remaining question is whether an explicit `--self` argument is required.

It seems to me that the _absence_ of any node IDs on the command line would be sufficient signal that the "self" behavior is requested. What do you think?

(Uneducated) preference for an explicit `--self`, makes it harder to get it wrong. I can imagine unintentionally not setting node IDs in bash scripts or the like, which would then go do something unintended.

review_comments: Is this roachtest testing v20.1 below? Where's that happening? (I thought it was only testing current HEAD, I don't see any multi-version machinery hooked up here.)
This roachtest tries the `--self` flag and then bails out from that part of the test if the flag is not supported. This will automatically fail-and-ignore for everything 20.1 or below.
